subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which default policy and implementation sequence should OpenClaw use to reduce model-facing tool-schema overhead without breaking cross-channel cron/isolated agents, provider schema contracts, or plugin/declarative tools?
rationale: The remaining work changes prompt/schema visibility and spans provider payloads, channel compatibility, Tool Search/deferred-schema semantics, plugin APIs, prompt-cache stability, and possible config defaults, so automation should not choose the product policy alone.

options.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
options.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

options.title: Defer To Focused Issues
options.body: Close the umbrella only after maintainers decide that all remaining work should move to narrower issues such as prompt-text skipping or deferred tool registration.

options.title: Adopt Aggressive Lazy Defaults
options.body: Make lazy or slim schemas the default sooner, accepting a broader compatibility and provider-contract review burden up front.

recommendation.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of current issue discussion context and history across the affected prompt/runtime/schema surfaces.
